notes:
Replication statistics are author-derived primary project-table values, preserved without conversion. No effect-specific narrative replication verdict located; numeric success indicators are not treated as narrative verdicts. Original-source rule applied: replication project citations/quoted original statistics were not substituted for original primary evidence. DOI landing 403; OpenAlex lists no OA PDF; author-upload ResearchGate 403; title searches found no accessible full primary paper.
Source follow-up: Published article supplied by licensed EBSCO PsycInfo service; title, authors, year and DOI verified in supplied text. Only original target examined. Statistics are printed correlations with positively scored rule-abiding conduct, not sign-converted correlations with antisocial behavior. Page 1170 states: “the conduct composite was scored in the opposite direction (ranging from poor to good conduct)”. The p value and r refer to the same concurrent Conduct cell. Target match remains unknown because the neutral description and p.7 locator do not explicitly select concurrent versus childhood conduct. The selected candidate is the higher-order MPQ Constraint scale: p.1166 says “This higher order trait is most related to the Big Five Conscientiousness trait”. The paper also identifies lower-order Control as similar to Big Five Conscientiousness (p.1172); Table 4 prints Control/concurrent Conduct .27***, Constraint/childhood Conduct .23**, and Control/childhood Conduct .21**. The supplied locator does not uniquely select Constraint rather than Control. No alternative cells are merged into the extracted candidate.
